entries.definition: An exemplar-based clustering procedure that fixes candidate component centers at every observed point, fits their simplex weights through a convex soft information-distortion objective, and derives a hard grouping from selected posterior-MAP exemplars.
entries.identity_notes: This is the Lashkari-Golland procedure, also described as convex mixture model clustering. Its data-derived exemplar dictionary and hard extraction policy specialize fixed-component weight EM and finite rate-distortion Blahut-Arimoto. It is distinct from moving-centroid k-means, neural balanced transport in SeLa, scale-persistence melting, and fusion-penalty methods also called convex clustering. evidence_sources.version: NIPS 2007 proceedings, volume 20; official eight-page PDF, internally numbered 1-8. All pages, figures, captions and references visually read.

claims.statement: For N indexed observations, fixed finite dissimilarities d_ij and beta>=0, set S_ij=exp(-beta*d_ij). Minimize J(q)=-(1/N)sum_i log(sum_j q_j S_ij) over simplex weights with positive initialization. With z_i=sum_j q_j S_ij, set r_ij=q_j S_ij/z_i and q_j_new=(1/N)sum_i r_ij. Equivalently, the row-conditional channel minimizes I(I;J)+beta*E[d_ij] with a uniform data-index source. A valid common-base component family additionally gives the stated mixture-likelihood interpretation; Gaussian components use squared Euclidean distance.

evidence.locator: Sections 2-4, PDF pp. 2-4, Equations 2, 4, 6-9; conditional normalization from Equations 6-8

claims.statement: For finite positive kernels and positive initialization, the exact unpruned iteration converges to a global optimum of the restricted soft weight objective. This is not a global fit of freely moving mixture components. Convexity does not imply unique coefficients: at beta=0 every q is fixed and optimal. Zero weights stay zero and can exclude useful exemplars; exact positive-kernel finite iterations preserve positive weights. At an optimum eta_j=(1/N)sum_i S_ij/z_i equals one on positive weights and is at most one on inactive coordinates, rather than necessarily strictly less.

evidence.locator: Section 2, PDF p. 3, Equation 4 and positive-support condition; Section 4, PDF p. 4, Equation 9; curator support and beta-zero checks

claims.statement: The 2007 visualization policy first selects every exemplar index that maximizes r_ij for at least one observation, then assigns each observation to its closest selected exemplar. Tie handling is not specified. This differs from the later multiview top-M policy. Beta controls the soft distortion tradeoff but does not uniquely determine a universally correct hard cluster count. Hardening does not retain the soft optimum guarantee or a general bound I<=log(K_hard): for points (0,1,3), squared distance and beta=1/4, the saved near-optimal soft solution has I about 0.03228 nats while this MAP policy selects only the middle point.

evidence.locator: Section 5, PDF p. 5, hard assignment and loss of optimality; Figure 1 caption; curator finite soft-channel/MAP calculation

claims.statement: The dense exact update uses two matrix-vector operations with O(N^2) work per iteration. The paper separately proposes deleting weights below 10^-3/N and renormalizing, and retaining only a rowwise subset of large similarities. These approximations can change the feasible set or objective and need not preserve the full soft optimum. The saved two-point example shows the stated pruning threshold removing a small but useful positive component.

evidence.locator: Section 4, PDF pp. 4-5, Equation 9, pruning and similarity sparsification; curator finite pruning example

claims.statement: The expression r_ij=q_j S_ij/(N z_i) after Equation 9 is joint data-index/exemplar mass, not the row-conditional r defined in Equation 6; the conditional omits N. Literal KL from an atomic empirical measure to a continuous density is not finite merely by evaluating that density at data points. The finite-index objective and normalized responsibilities above avoid transferring that common-measure ambiguity from Equation 3.

evidence.locator: Section 2, PDF p. 3, Equation 3; Section 3, Equations 6-8; Section 4, PDF p. 4, expression after Equation 9; curator normalization checks

limitations: Sparsity at an asymptotic limit, numerical pruning, and the selected hard exemplars are different notions. Neither every beta change nor every initialization produces a distinct optimum.

Natural-log objectives use nats; bit rates require consistent log-base and multiplier conversion. A slope statement for the rate-distortion curve needs differentiability or a supporting-slope interpretation.
Synthetic source comparisons tune beta using class labels and do not establish universal performance or a biological application. No historical software or benchmark was reproduced.

evidence_sources.title: Convex Mixture Models for Multi-view Clustering
evidence_sources.version: ICANN 2009, Part II, LNCS 5769, pp. 205-214; author-hosted ten-page proceedings PDF. All pages visually read; printed page = PDF page + 204.

claims.statement: For N observations with V aligned views, fix view-specific component values f_vij=f_vj(x_vi) and common simplex weights q_j. Minimize -(1/(N V))sum_vi log Q_vi, where Q_vi=sum_j q_j f_vij. Set q_j_new=q_j/(N V)*sum_vi f_vij/Q_vi. Each view contributes its average current responsibilities equally. Common factors depending on the view and observation but not the exemplar cancel in this update. With finite positive component values, positive support and exact unpruned iteration, the soft convex problem attains a global optimum; coefficient uniqueness is not implied.

evidence.locator: Sections 3.1-3.2, printed pp. 208-209 / PDF pp. 4-5, Equations 6-9 and support condition

claims.statement: Given a requested M, retain the M largest fitted q values as exemplars, each anchoring its own cluster. Assign every other observation to the selected exemplar maximizing sum_v q_j f_vij/Q_vi. This sums per-view posteriors, rather than multiplying densities or taking the maximum over individual views. The source uses strict comparisons without a tie policy. Its implementation stops when the selected top-M indices and their ranking stay unchanged for several consecutive iterations; this can occur before the soft objective is optimized.

evidence.locator: Section 3.2, printed pp. 209-210 / PDF pp. 5-6, stopping discussion and Equation 10

claims.statement: View families and beta_v values remain supplied choices. The empirical scale N^2 log(N)/sum_ij d_vij is a search guide and is undefined when its denominator vanishes. The fitting update needs O(N^2 V) dense arithmetic per iteration, apart from distance construction. A fixed-M hard partition has no transferred global-optimum guarantee; stable ranking is not a bound on residual objective error. Equal view contribution also does not guarantee robustness to uninformative or systematically biased views.

evidence.locator: Section 3.2, printed p. 210 / PDF p. 6, Equation 11 and cost; Sections 4-5, printed pp. 210-214 / PDF pp. 6-10; curator stable-ranking example

limitations: The record uses the finite evaluated-component/log-likelihood objective; the source empirical-versus-continuous KL shorthand requires a compatible measure or lift. Gaussian exponents use squared Euclidean distances.
The soft fit is a shared-weight specialization of fixed-component EM. The complete multiview data construction, equal-view objective and sum-of-posteriors/top-M policy define this narrower algorithm.

Source experiments remove observations lacking required views and select scale multipliers by label entropy. They do not establish an intrinsic missing-view algorithm, fully label-free model selection, or universal performance. No historical experiment was reproduced.

evidence_sources.title: Multiple View Clustering Using a Weighted Combination of Exemplar-Based Mixture Models
evidence_sources.version: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks 21(12):1925-1938, December 2010. Author-hosted journal PDF; all 14 pages, tables and appendices visually read. Printed page = PDF page + 1924.

claims.statement: Given fixed positive component values f_vij, let Q_vi(q)=sum_j q_j f_vij and maximize L(q,pi)=sum_i log(sum_v pi_v Q_vi(q)) with q and pi on their respective simplices. From the current parameters compute gamma_iv=pi_v Q_vi/sum_w pi_w Q_wi. Set pi_v_new=(1/N)sum_i gamma_iv. Hold these outer responsibilities fixed while iterating q_j <- q_j/N*sum_iv gamma_iv f_vij/Q_vi(q), using the current inner q in the denominator. Repeat inner updates to their stated tolerance, then recompute outer responsibilities. The paper starts both weight vectors uniformly and uses inner L1-change and outer objective-change stopping conditions.

evidence.locator: Section IV-B, printed p. 1929 / PDF p. 5, Equations 11-13 and Algorithm 1; Appendix A, printed pp. 1936-1937 / PDF pp. 12-13, Equations 22-28

claims.statement: The objective is separately concave in either weight vector with the other fixed, but not jointly concave in general. The nested surrogate updates support objective ascent for admissible exact arithmetic; a finite inner tolerance is an approximate M-step. Uniform starts, small objective changes or successful source examples do not prove global optimality, a unique limit, or that every stationary outcome is a local maximum. Uniform pi also leaves a log-of-sum objective, not the unweighted sum-of-logs objective.

evidence.locator: Section IV-B, printed pp. 1928-1929 / PDF pp. 4-5; Appendix A, printed pp. 1936-1937 / PDF pp. 12-13; curator two-view objective/update comparison

claims.statement: The source writes a sum of marginal densities Q_v(x_v) as a density of the full view tuple. That sum is not automatically normalized on the product observation space without an appropriate common observation model or background factors. For two- and three-state view alphabets, its total mass is 3*pi_1+2*pi_2. The finite positive-score objective still has meaningful normalized responsibilities and surrogate updates, but does not by itself establish the asserted generative interpretation. View-specific density scales affect the learned pi; they are not pure measures of semantic view quality.

evidence.locator: Section IV-A, printed p. 1928 / PDF p. 4, Equation 9; Appendix A, printed p. 1936 / PDF p. 12, Equations 17-21; curator product-mass and coordinate-rescaling examples

claims.statement: The general outer gamma calculation retains C_v(x_vi) from f_vij=C_v(x_vi)exp(-beta_v*d_vij). These factors cancel within the inner q update but not generally across views in gamma. The experiments explicitly omit them from the outer update to work from distances alone; this optimizes a modified affinity-score objective unless the factors cancel across views. With exp(-beta*||x-m||^2), the normalized Gaussian factor is (beta/pi)^(d/2), rather than the printed (beta/(2*pi))^(d/2). Source benchmark results for omitted factors do not certify the normalized-density formulation.

evidence.locator: Section IV-B, printed p. 1929 / PDF p. 5, third implementation remark; Section V-A, printed p. 1930 / PDF p. 6, Gaussian factor and explicit removal; curator Gaussian-integral check

claims.statement: After fitting, select a specified M largest-q exemplars and anchor each to its own cluster. Assign other observations by maximizing q_j sum_v pi_v f_vij among the selected exemplars. The full-component denominator is shared and cancels for this comparison; the selected-subset scores need not sum to one as M-cluster probabilities without renormalization. Ties need an explicit policy. Dense training costs O(N^2 V tau tau_inner), excluding initial distances. Kernel squared distances can supply a feature-space realization, but a generic dissimilarity matrix does not automatically establish a normalized feature-space density.

evidence.locator: Section IV-B, printed pp. 1929-1930 / PDF pp. 5-6, Equations 14-15; Section IV-C, PDF p. 6; Appendix B, printed p. 1937 / PDF p. 13, Equations 29-34

limitations: All views must be aligned to the same observation and exemplar indices. The source explicitly does not model general dependence between views and notes failures with systematic inter-view bias.

The number of final exemplars and each component scale remain supplied choices. Hard assignment is separate from soft fitting and has no global clustering guarantee. Zero weights remain excluded; positivity and nonzero denominators matter.

The empirical comparisons use complete-view filtering, specified cluster counts, label-based scale selection and optional kernel-k-means fine-tuning. They do not establish general noise immunity, semantic calibration of view weights, or universal superiority. No author software or historical benchmark was reproduced.

lashkari.title: Convex Clustering with Exemplar-Based Models
lashkari.version: NIPS 2007 proceedings PDF, eight internally numbered pages; conference volume20.
lashkari.abstract_interpretation: Proposes restricting mixture component centers to all observations and fitting their simplex weights, making the soft clustering objective convex. The author global-optimum claim belongs to this restricted soft problem, not arbitrary mixture fitting or hard clustering.
method_notes: Sections1-2 PDF1-3: every observation is a fixed candidate component center; the number of permitted components is n, not a selected k-subset. For shared component shape/scale and valid common-base exponential-family representation, maximize the average log of sum_j q_j exp(-beta*d_ij). This is fixed-component weight EM with a data-derived component dictionary.

Section3 PDF3-4 Eq6-8: uniform data-index source and conditional exemplar assignments r_ij give mutual information plus beta times average distortion. At fixed q, r_ij=q_j*s_ij/z_i; q_j is the column mean of r. This is the finite rate-distortion BA specialization with reproduction alphabet equal to the observed exemplars. Mutual information is convex in the channel with the data source fixed.

Section4 PDF4 Eq9: s_ij=exp(-beta*d_ij), z=S q, eta_j=(1/n)sum_i s_ij/z_i, q_new=q*eta. Exact dense iteration has O(n^2) arithmetic and needs positive weights on all allowed candidates. Source reports stopping on max_j log eta_j minus sum_j q_j log eta_j.

Sections4-5 PDF4-5: optional per-step threshold q_j<10^-3/n followed by renormalization permanently prunes candidates. Rowwise top-n0 proximity sparsification is a second approximation. Neither is the untouched full-support exact algorithm. Hard visualization first collects exemplars that are a row posterior MAP for at least one point, then assigns points to their closest selected exemplar; tie policy is not specified.

Section5 PDF5-7: beta is externally selected/tuned, not an automatically inferred universal cluster count. Source explicitly observes hard-count fluctuations and loss of soft global-optimality guarantees. Synthetic comparisons select the best precision among five beta choices using known labels; no general superiority or real biological evaluation claim will be curated.

Section6 PDF7-8 extends the fixed-source information/distortion objective to symmetric or asymmetric proximity matrices. The Gaussian/exponential-family likelihood interpretation requires additional valid-density structure; arbitrary proximities alone do not supply a normalized component family. Affinity propagation has a different combinatorial objective and message updates.
curator_qualifications: PDF2 calls Euclidean distance a Bregman divergence and Gaussian exponent. The Gaussian squared-norm formulation uses squared Euclidean distance; exp(-beta*norm(x-m)) is not a Gaussian. Verify a scalar example before writing.

PDF3 Eq3 treats the atomic empirical law and a continuous mixture density as if their KL were finite. Literal measure-theoretic KL is infinite without an appropriate common measure/lift. Ground the record in the finite-index objective and actual density likelihood, not that literal equality.
PDF4 after Eq9 prints r_ij=q_j*s_ij/(n*z_i), although PDF3 defines r as row-conditional probabilities. That expression is the joint index mass; row conditionals omit n. Verify row sums.

PDF4 says eta outside support is strictly less than1. KKT permits equality for inactive coordinates, and an arbitrary boundary fixed point may even have eta>1 on excluded candidates. Positive-support exact iteration and global optimality must be distinguished.

PDF2 claims unconditional convergence, while PDF3 explicitly requires positive initialization. Convexity by itself does not guarantee arbitrary iteration convergence or uniqueness. At beta0 all kernels are1 and every initial q is a fixed optimum; duplicated candidates also permit nonunique coefficients.

PDF4 claims every beta yields a different sparse solution/nonzero count. With finite positive kernels and positive initialization, all weights remain positive for every finite exact iteration; asymptotic zeros, numerical pruning and hard exemplars are different. Beta0 and equal similarities refute universal parameter-dependent uniqueness/sparsity.

PDF4 slope -beta is a differentiable-point statement (or supporting slope), not proof global differentiability of the rate-distortion curve. Entropy/mutual-information units depend on log base; natural exponential formulas use nats with consistent beta.

PDF5 Fig1 caption claims rate bounded by log of hard-cluster count. The general inequality is I<=H(q)<=log support(q) for the same soft channel, not automatically the smaller postprocessed hard count. No general hard-count bound will be transferred.

PDF7 synthetic centers are sqrt50 times basis vectors, so pairwise squared distance100 and Euclidean distance10, despite prose pairwise distance50. No numerical benchmark geometry claim will be curated.
PDF8 reference10 gives Blahut1974 but the title/volume18/pages460-473 correspond to the previously verified1972paper. No mechanism claim will rely on this bibliographic year.

tzortzis2009.title: Convex Mixture Models for Multi-view Clustering
tzortzis2009.version: ICANN 2009 PartII, LNCS5769, pp205-214; ten-page author-hosted proceedings PDF.
tzortzis2009.abstract_interpretation: Extends fixed exemplar mixture fitting to any supplied number of aligned views while retaining a convex shared-weight objective. View distributions and widths may differ. The full clustering procedure still requires a requested exemplar count and postprocessing.
method_notes: Section2 PDF2-4 reprises single-view CMM; the original2007hard-exemplar policy differs from the fixed-M policy used here.

Section3.1 PDF4-5 Eq5-8: each view has fixed candidate components indexed by the same N observations and common q weights; minimize the sum of negative average per-view log mixture values. Update q with the average responsibilities across all N*V observation-view pairs, retaining positive initialization on all admissible exemplars. Different valid exponential families and beta values are allowed.

Section3.2 PDF5-6 Eq9: S_vij=exp(-beta_v*d_vij); Z_iv=sum_j S_vij*q_j; eta_j=1/(N*V)sum_iv S_vij/Z_iv; q_new=q*eta. Parameter-independent common view/observation factors cancel. Dense step O(N^2*V), plus distance construction.

Section3.2 PDF5-6 stopping: stop when the M largest weights select the same exemplars in the same order for an unspecified number of consecutive iterations. This ranking-stability condition is not an objective-gap certificate.

Section3.2 Eq10 PDF6: force each selected exemplar to anchor itself, assign every other instance to the selected exemplar maximizing SUM over views of its per-view posterior q_j*f_vij/Q_vi. It is neither a product of view densities nor a maximum over single views. The strict comparison leaves tied scores without a stated policy.
Section3.2 Eq11 PDF6: beta0_v=N^2*logN/sum_ij d_vij supplies only an empirical search scale; beta_v and M remain choices, and a zero denominator requires separate handling.

Section4 PDF6-9: synthetic corruptions and WebKB/Citeseer document data, Gaussian squared distances, complete-view filtering, specified M matching class counts, and selected beta multipliers by minimum label entropy. No universal superiority or missing-view method is established.
Section5 PDF9-10: automatic view weighting is future work in this2009version; it is addressed by the distinct nonconvex2010procedure. References read as leads only.
curator_qualifications: Use the actual finite log-score/density objective; empirical point masses do not have finite ordinary measure KL to a continuous density merely by evaluating that density.

Global soft weight optimum under positive support does not imply a unique coefficient vector, optimal top-M subset, exact objective convergence at the ranking stop, or globally optimal hard partition.
Equal contribution in a sum of view log likelihoods is distinct from fixing equal view weights inside the later log-of-a-sum objective.
Retain the original sum-of-posteriors assignment rule and specified M, which resolve the ambiguity in the2010summary.

tzortzis2010.title: Multiple View Clustering Using a Weighted Combination of Exemplar-Based Mixture Models
tzortzis2010.version: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks21(12):1925-1938, December2010; publication October7,2010, current version November30,2010 as printed.
tzortzis2010.abstract_interpretation: Learns shared exemplar weights and view weights to reduce the effect of uninformative views. The authors explicitly acknowledge that learning view weights loses convexity. Uniform starts and comparative experiments do not provide a universal global optimum or noise rejection guarantee.
method_notes: SectionII PDF2: identifies separate centralized/distributed multiview methods, co-EM and kernel approaches. These are references only, not newly inspected primary methods.

SectionIII-A PDF3 Eq1-4 reprises fixed exemplar density mixture and single-view multiplicative weight fit. SectionIII-B PDF3-4 Eq5-8 gives unweighted multiview objective: sum over views of negative average log Q_v, common q simplex but view-specific fixed component distributions and beta_v. The update averages per-view responsibilities with factor1/(N V). Density common-base factors cancel in each view. The source uses top M fitted exemplar weights and assigns remaining points to their highest posterior over all views; the precise original2009rule is being sought.

SectionIV-A/B PDF4-5 Eq9-13, Algorithm1: positive per-view values f_vj(x_vi), Q_vi=sum_j q_j f_vij; objective L=sum_i log(sum_v pi_v Q_vi). Shared q and pi each lie on a simplex. Outer E-step gamma_iv=pi_v Q_vi / sum_w pi_w Q_wi. Update pi to mean gamma. Hold old outer gamma fixed while repeatedly updating q_j <- q_j/N sum_iv gamma_iv f_vij/Q_vi(q) until inner L1 change below epsilon-prime, then next outer E-step. The objective is not jointly concave. An inner update that improves its bound supports ascent but finite tolerance is not exact maximization.

SectionIV-B PDF5-6 Eq14-15: select a specified M largest-q instances; each is forced to represent its own cluster. Assign other points by maximum q_j sum_v pi_v f_vij over the selected exemplars (common denominator cancels). Ties are unspecified; printed strict comparisons do not assign tied points. The selected-subset scores divided by full N-component denominator need not sum to1 over M clusters.

SectionIV-C PDF6: kernel squared distance K_ii+K_jj-2K_ij supports a feature-space variant with valid inner-product kernels. Dense training cost O(N^2 V tau tau-prime), plus distance construction. General view-density base factors remain in outer gamma, though cancel in q updates.

SectionV-A PDF6: experiments deliberately remove C_v(x_vi) from the outer E-step as though it cancelled, to support distance-only input when dimensions are unknown. This is a distinct affinity-score objective unless all relevant factors coincide; it is not the general normalized-density objective. All experiment runs used one uniform start. Kernel-k-means fine-tuning is a separate postprocessing stage.

SectionV PDF7-11: synthetic noisy/uncorrupted views, WebKb and InternetAdvertisement datasets. Real experiments retain complete cases, choose M from known class counts or supplied alternative counts, and tune beta multipliers using label entropy. The statement labels are used only after training does not mean an entirely label-free model-selection protocol. Tables include cases where a single-view or unweighted method wins. No blanket performance claim is supported.

SectionVI PDF11-12: authors qualify systematic inter-view bias and inability to explicitly model view dependence. A coupled transcriptomic/proteomic clustering paper is a separate lead. Their one-start success does not prove restarts unnecessary in all cases.

AppendixA PDF12-13 Eq17-28 derives the outer view responsibilities and nested shared-q update through the surrogate. AppendixB Eq29-34 derives exemplar scores. PDF14 contains references and author biographies; no additional algorithm.
curator_qualifications: Eq9/17 adds densities defined on distinct view spaces as a function of the full view tuple. Without specified background factors or common observation model, this is not automatically a normalized density on the product space. A finite2-by3 alphabet gives total mass3*pi_1+2*pi_2, and continuous unbounded unused coordinates can make the integral infinite. The numerical score objective and Jensen-type ascent can still be recorded with that explicit limit.

Uniform pi in the weighted log-of-sum objective does not recover the unweighted sum-of-logs objective, except special cases. Distinguish the two algorithms even though both reduce to single-view fitting at V1.

PDF6 writes Gaussian constant(beta/(2*pi))^(d/2) alongside exp(-beta*||x-m||^2); the latter normalizes with(beta/pi)^(d/2). The experiments omit constants, so they cannot certify normalized-density outcomes. Preserve exponent/normalizer consistency in any curator illustration.

Learned pi values depend on view-density scales/units or affinity calibration, not only latent semantic quality. Scaling one view coordinate changes its density normalization and relative contribution; unweighted fitting instead drops its parameter-independent log factor.

Literal empirical-atomic versus continuous-density KL in Eq2/6 has the same common-measure caveat as the2007source; use finite score/log-likelihood expressions for the maintained method.
